awd_titl_txt: Conference: NSF Student Travel Grant for 2024 IEEE Global Communication Conference (IEEE GLOBECOM 2024)
awd_abstract_narration:
IEEE GLOBECOM is one of the two flagship conferences of the IEEE Communications Society (ComSoc), together with IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC). IEEE GLOBECOM 2024 will take place in Cape Town, South Africa, from 8-12 December 2024. This project funds undergraduate or graduate students from US universities to attend IEEE GLOBECOM. Attending such a high-caliber technical venue is extremely valuable for students. Not only will they be exposed to the state-of-the-art research areas, but they also can have the opportunity to interact with peers from institutions worldwide, meet with leading researchers from both industry and academia, and take part in discussions that may shape the future of the field. For graduating senior students to be on the job market, attending the conference may significantly benefit their career development. Applications are invited from qualified full-time US-based graduate and undergraduate students. Women and underrepresented groups will be encouraged to apply for this travel grant, in order to promote participation in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) fields.

The requested support will cover 16 students, leading to a total of $20,000. Applications are invited from qualified full-time US-based engineering graduate and undergraduate students. Women and other underrepresented groups in STEM, beginning graduate students, and first time IEEE GLOBECOM student attendees will be especially encouraged to apply for this travel grant.



Please report errors in award information by writing to: awardsearch@nsf.gov.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

Project Outcomes: 

This project funded five undergraduate or graduate engineering students from U.S. universities to attend IEEE GLOBECOM 2024, selected from a pool of eight NSF applicants. Each awardee received $1,250 to cover the majority of their travel and registration expenses.

The selection criteria were as follows: Applications were invited from qualified full-time, U.S. based undergraduate and graduate engineering students. Applicants were required to be authors presenting an accepted paper at the main conference. Among authors of accepted IEEE GLOBECOM papers, preference has traditionally been given to papers with higher review scores. Additional criteria were used to resolve ties and to consider factors such as financial need (to support students who would otherwise be unable to attend IEEE GLOBECOM) and diversity. In particular, the selection committee gave higher priority to female students; students from underrepresented minority groups or institutions; beginning graduate students; and first-time GLOBECOM attendees who are not traditionally represented at IEEE GLOBECOM. The announcement for the NSF Student Travel Grant for IEEE GLOBECOM 2024 explicitly stated: “Women, underrepresented minorities, beginning graduate students, and first-time GLOBECOM attendees are especially encouraged to apply.”

To ensure broad distribution of support, no more than one student per institution was funded. Postdocs, faculty, and other senior research personnel were not eligible for support under this grant. Students supported by NSF funds were required to be 18 years of age or older. To avoid conflicts of interest, students advised by members of the selection committee were not considered for the award.

 

Intellectual Merit: 

 IEEE GLOBECOM is one of the two flagship conferences of the IEEE Communications Society (ComSoc), together with the IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC). IEEE GLOBECOM 2024 was held in Cape Town, South Africa, on December 8–12, 2024. This project aimed to fund undergraduate and graduate students from U.S. universities, regardless of citizenship or visa status, to attend this premier technical venue.

Participation in a high-caliber international conference is extremely valuable for students. They are exposed to state-of-the-art research, interact with peers from institutions worldwide, meet leading researchers from industry and academia, and engage in discussions that help shape future research directions. For senior students entering the job market, attending GLOBECOM can significantly enhance career development by enabling professional networking and increasing the visibility of their research.

Applications are invited from qualified full-time US-based graduate and undergraduate students. Women and underrepresented minorities are encouraged for apply for this travel grant, in order to promote woman and underrepresented minorities in the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM). 

 

Broader Impacts: 

IEEE GLOBECOM is one of the most significant scientific events of the networking and communications community, a must-attend event for scientists, researchers and networking practitioners from industry and academia. IEEE GLOBECOM 2024 took place in Cape Town, South Africa, on December 8-12 2024.This project supported undergraduate and graduate engineering students from U.S. universities to attend IEEE GLOBECOM 2024 regardless of their citizenship/visa status.

By attending GLOBECOM, students gain exposure to cutting-edge research in communications and networking and have opportunities to interact with peers and senior researchers worldwide. They also benefit from professional networking, including meeting potential employers, discussing job opportunities, presenting their research, showcasing their capabilities, and developing professional contacts who may serve as future references. For graduating seniors, these interactions can substantially impact career trajectories.

The project requested $1,250 per student to help defray travel and registration costs. Applications were open to full-time, U.S.-based engineering undergraduate and graduate students. Applicants were required to be authors presenting an accepted paper at the main conference. Women, underrepresented minorities, beginning graduate students, and first-time IEEE GLOBECOM attendees were especially encouraged to apply.
